title: C major in one position
aim: Connect the C major shape on the fretboard to the note names you play.
meta: Leith Bass Space · Beginner · Four-string bass in standard tuning

blocks.text: A scale is a set of notes, and a *shape* is one way of finding them on the neck. This shape starts on C at the third fret of the A string and stays in one position: your first finger covers fret 2, your little finger covers fret 5, and you never need to slide.

blocks.title: Figure 1. The shape
blocks.caption: Square markers show C, the root. Every other marker is a scale note.

items: Play the shape slowly, saying each note name out loud as you play it.
Keep your first finger resting over fret 2, so your hand stays in position.
When the names feel familiar, start from the top C and name each note on the way down before you play it.

blocks.label: Listen for
blocks.text: the pull from B back up to C at the top of the scale. Let each note ring until the next one starts.
Here is the same shape written out, first going up and then coming back down. Every note has its name and a suggested finger beneath it, then its fret in the TAB.

blocks.title: Figure 2. Up and back down
blocks.caption: Orange numbers are fretting-hand fingers: 1 index, 2 middle, 3 ring, 4 little finger.
